name: Player List Header Footer
desc: Sets text above and below the tab player list.

writeup.p: The server paints arbitrary text above and below the tab list. Two IChatComponent JSON strings (header, footer) arrive whenever the server wants to update the display: restart notices, rules, game-state text. The packet is clientbound-only, PLAY state, and generates no reply. It is pure presentation state pushed from the server, with no client-controlled round trip.

NetHandlerPlayClient.handlePlayerListHeaderFooter writes the header and footer into GuiPlayerTabOverlay; when the formatted text is empty the field is set to null, which hides that line. Nothing is sent back, so there is no packet the client can influence, delay or spoof.

None of the 8 clients ships a module that intercepts S47. The only non-vanilla reference in the corpus is the Rise 6.1.30 and 6.2.4 script API (NetworkAPI), which registers the class in the packet list exposed to JavaScript so user scripts can attach receive handlers. Memeware, Nekoware, Sigma, Spicy and Tenacity touch only the bundled net/minecraft handler. The packet offers no timing, state or spoofing advantage, which is exactly why module authors ignore it.

The content is untrusted server JSON rendered into the tab GUI. Malformed JSON is caught by the chat-component reader, but very long header or footer text and deep component nesting stress the client renderer. No client in the corpus exploits or defends against this; the packet is not a cheating surface.

implementation.overview: A pure presentation packet with zero module coverage in the 8 clients: modules is empty because no module file in the corpus references S47. The only non-vanilla hit is the Rise 6.x NetworkAPI script registry listing the class so user scripts can hook it.
implementation.server_handling: Server side, the packet is constructed from chat components and pushed via sendPacket; there is no server-side processing of a reply because none exists. The header and footer are typically rebuilt by plugins on a timer or on state change.
implementation.protocol_notes: Two chat components read via readChatComponent (VarInt length prefix plus JSON UTF-8). The vanilla handler nulls a field when its formatted text length is 0, so an empty string hides the line instead of rendering blank space. Wire cost is the two JSON strings and their length prefixes.
implementation.anticheat_landscape: No anti-cheat measures this packet: it has no timing value and no client response. The only related concern is client-side stability under hostile JSON, which is a client defense topic rather than an anti-cheat one.
implementation.general_hooks: Rise 6.1.30 and 6.2.4 expose S47 to scripts through NetworkAPI's packet registry; no event bus in any of the 8 clients has a module handler for it.
implementation.client_variations: Only Rise 6.x differs from vanilla: its NetworkAPI packet list includes S47PacketPlayerListHeaderFooter.class. All other clients carry the unmodified NetHandlerPlayClient handler.
